summary: The HR condition is the sole hot-rolled sheet of Fe–10Al–15Mn–0.8C–5Ni wt% low-density steel, produced by vacuum arc melting, homogenization at 1150 °C for 2 h, and standard slow (1 rpm) hot rolling from 14 to 3 mm. It serves as the baseline hot-rolled state for studying how as-cast δ-ferrite dendrites transform into lamellar B2 stringer bands and how those bands govern the alloy's strength–ductility balance and premature fracture.
composition: The nominal composition is Fe–15Mn–10Al–0.8C–5Ni in wt% (equivalently written Fe–10Al–15Mn–0.8C–5Ni), with Fe as the matrix element. Al (~10 wt%) is added as a ferrite stabilizer to reduce density (about 1.2% density reduction per 1 wt% Al), while Mn (15 wt%) and C (0.8 wt%) stabilize austenite. Ni (5 wt%) is nominally a γ stabilizer but partitions into the ordered B2 phase; by replacing some Fe–Al bonds with stronger Ni–Al bonds it helps stabilize the nonshearable B2 (Fe(Ni,Mn)Al) second phase. No at% composition is reported.
processing: The alloy was vacuum arc melted from elemental constituents at 10⁻⁵ mbar backfilled with argon and remelted 5–6 times for better elemental intermixing. The ingot was homogenized at 1150 °C for 2 h in a muffle furnace, then hot rolled in a 75-ton mill from 14 to 3 mm thickness in nine passes, starting at 1050 °C and finishing at 900 °C, followed by air cooling. This standard (slow, 1 rpm) hot rolling route is the parent process of the HR sample; the air-cooled hot-rolled sheet was not subsequently cold rolled or annealed in this condition.
microstructure: The hot-rolled sheet consists of a two-phase microstructure: an FCC austenite (γ) matrix containing lamellar B2 stringer bands (ordered BCC, Fe(Ni,Mn)Al) transformed from the as-cast δ-ferrite dendrites. In optical microscopy the B2 stringer bands appear as near-horizontal light lamellae separated by the γ matrix and span multiple austenite grains. Image analysis estimates the dendrite/B2 stringer fraction at ~19% after hot rolling, reduced from 27% in the as-cast condition. During hot deformation the γ matrix undergoes plastic flow and develops shear bands, and fine-scale intragranular B2 (IG-B2) particles heterogeneously nucleate on those shear bands. No grain size or texture data are reported for the HR condition.
properties: Room-temperature uniaxial tensile testing (ASTM E8, rolling direction; gauge length 12.5 mm, gauge width 3 mm, thickness 2 mm; 1 mm min⁻¹ crosshead velocity on a 100 kN Instron 5982 with a 10 mm gauge extensometer) shows that the HR condition reaches a peak/ultimate tensile stress between 900 and 1200 MPa but only ~6.8% elongation, with an absorbed energy (tensile toughness) of 0.48 kJ mol⁻¹ (66.5 J cm⁻³). Yield strength was not reported. The HR sheet was characterized by optical microscopy (Leica DM2700 M, 3% nital etch), FESEM (Apreo S), image analysis, and uniaxial tensile testing.
mechanisms: Homogenization at 1150 °C (above the ~1125 °C δ→B2 order–disorder transition) enables solute partitioning from γ that transforms the as-cast δ-ferrite dendrites into ordered B2, an Fe(Ni,Mn)Al intermetallic.

Nine-pass hot rolling between 1050 and 900 °C deforms the B2 dendrites into lamellar stringer bands spanning multiple austenite grains and partially dissolves them, lowering the dendrite/B2 stringer fraction from ~27% (as-cast) to ~19% (HR) in accordance with the equilibrium phase fractions.

During hot deformation, strain localizes in the softer γ matrix as shear bands, and these shear bands act as heterogeneous nucleation sites for fine intragranular B2, which relieves the local lattice strain.

In the standard HR condition the relatively thick B2 stringer bands act as crack initiation sites: macrovoids nucleate inside the B2 stringer bands and coalesce, and B2 stringer de-cohesion plus microcrack coalescence lead to premature failure, explaining the poor strength–ductility balance (~6.8% elongation and 0.48 kJ mol⁻¹ toughness) of the sole HR sample.
conclusions: The standard HR condition alone exhibits a poor strength–ductility balance—nearly 6.8% ductility and 0.48 kJ mol⁻¹ (66.5 J cm⁻³) toughness—because the coarse B2 stringer bands promote void nucleation and premature fracture. Compared with cold rolling, hot rolling is nevertheless key for refining the δ-derived B2 stringer bands without cracking the metal sheet, and it demonstrates that this low-density steel can be flattened and rolled by conventional metallurgy. A modified high-speed (10 rpm) hot rolling plus annealing route subsequently raised the yield strength to 1 GPa, elongation to 30%, and toughness to 1.72 kJ mol⁻¹ (238 J cm⁻³), underscoring that the standard HR sample is the baseline from which process control is required to delay fracture.
